title: Quantum-Seeded Distributed Post-Quantum Group Signatures for 5G V2X Communications
authors: P. Blanco-Casal, P. Rejo-Iglesias, D. Cajaraville-Aboy, J. Vecino-Peñas, R. P. Díaz-Redondo, A. Fernández-Vilas, M. Fernández Veiga
abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications rely on elliptic-curve signatures that a quantum adversary breaks and on pseudonym certificates whose anonymity rests on rotation rate, not cryptography. This work presents qDGSP, a post-quantum V2X infrastructure: a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP, over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+) distributed between a central controller and roadside verifiers. Group keys derive deterministically from quantum key distribution (QKD) seeds served over the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, so no group-signature secret crosses the classical channel. qDGSP-EA (Ephemeral Association) binds an ephemeral ML-DSA-65 key to one group signature per 5G cell: messages remain unlinkable across cells, linkable within one. On a testbed with emulated 5G links, median end-to-end latency stayed within the 100ms ETSI budget for every variant. The qDGSP-EA intra-cell DENM matched the NIST ML-DSA-65 baseline on the wire, and under load EA mode raised delivery from roughly 78% to 93%.
summary: This paper introduces qDGSP, a quantum-seeded distributed post-quantum group signature scheme designed to secure V2X communications against quantum attacks. It uses QKD seeds to derive group keys, ensuring security while maintaining low latency and high reliability in simulated 5G environments. The key innovation, qDGSP-EA, reduces cryptographic overhead for intra-cell messaging.
main_problem: Current V2X communications are vulnerable to quantum adversaries using elliptic-curve signatures, and anonymity relies only on certificate rotation rate.
main_result: The proposed qDGSP-EA scheme maintains low latency (within 100ms ETSI budget) and significantly improves message delivery rates under load by using ephemeral keys.
method: The authors designed and tested a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (qDGSP) that deterministically seeds group keys using QKD material.
model_or_system: The system models Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications across multiple virtual subnetworks (fronthaul, core, backhaul) and integrates with ETSI ITS standards.
key_observables: Median end-to-end latency, message delivery rate, wire size, and computational cost.
important_parameters: 100ms ETSI latency budget, 5G cell structure, and the number of alerts ($M$).
main_assumptions: The scheme assumes a passive observer threat model and relies on the trustworthiness of the QKD network and backhaul.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate on-demand group creation via deterministic seeding and the three phases of the qDGSP-EA process (Identity anchoring, EA Announce–ACK, Intra-cell emission).
paper_structure: The paper details the problem, proposes qDGSP, describes the deterministic seeding mechanism, presents the qDGSP-EA optimization, and validates performance using a testbed simulating realistic network conditions.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
